'''Pierre Gönczy''' (born 1962 in [[Winterthur]], [[Switzerland]]) is a [[Switzerland|Swiss]] and [[Italians|Italian]] [[Cell biology|cell and developmental biologist]]. His research focuses on [[centriole]] biology and asymmetric cell division. He is currently professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL),<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Pierre Gönczy|url=https://people.epfl.ch/pierre.gonczy/?lang=en|access-date=2020-09-15|website=people.epfl.ch}}</ref> where he directs the Laboratory of Cell and Developmental Biology.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gönczy Lab – Cell and Developmental Biology|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/gonczy-lab/|access-date=2020-09-15|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Career ==
Gönczy studied [[biology]] at [[University of Geneva]] and graduated in 1987 with a [[Thesis|diploma thesis]] in [[molecular]] [[immunology]] at the Department of Microbiology at [[University of Geneva]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gönczy|first1=P|last2=Reith|first2=W|last3=Barras|first3=E|last4=Lisowska-Grospierre|first4=B|last5=Griscelli|first5=C|last6=Hadam|first6=M R|last7=Mach|first7=B|date=1989-01-01|title=Inherited immunodeficiency with a defect in a major histocompatibility complex class II promoter-binding protein differs in the chromatin structure of the HLA-DRA gene.|journal=Molecular and Cellular Biology|language=en|volume=9|issue=1|pages=296–302|doi=10.1128/MCB.9.1.296|issn=0270-7306|pmc=362172|pmid=2467188}}</ref> In 1995, he received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] for his work on [[developmental biology]] and [[molecular genetics]] from the [[Rockefeller University]], [[New York City]], United States.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Trelsman|first1=Jessica|last2=Gönczy|first2=Pierre|last3=Vashishtha|first3=Malini|last4=Harris|first4=Esther|last5=Desplan|first5=Claude|date=1989-11-03|title=A single amino acid can determine the DNA binding specificity of homeodomain proteins|journal=Cell|language=en|volume=59|issue=3|pages=553–562|doi=10.1016/0092-8674(89)90038-X|pmid=2572327|s2cid=29300056}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Castrillon|first1=D. H.|last2=Gonczy|first2=P.|last3=Alexander|first3=S.|last4=Rawson|first4=R.|last5=Eberhart|first5=C. G.|last6=Viswanathan|first6=S.|last7=DiNardo|first7=S.|last8=Wasserman|first8=S. A.|date=1993-10-01|title=Toward a Molecular Genetic Analysis of Spermatogenesis in Drosophila Melanogaster: Characterization of Male-Sterile Mutants Generated by Single P Element Mutagenesis|journal=Genetics|volume=135|issue=2|pages=489–505|doi=10.1093/genetics/135.2.489 |issn=0016-6731|pmc=1205651|pmid=8244010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Gonczy|first=P|date=1994-07-01|title=roughex is a dose-dependent regulator of the second meiotic division during Drosophila spermatogenesis|journal=Cell|language=en|volume=77|issue=7|pages=1015–1025|doi=10.1016/0092-8674(94)90441-3|pmid=8020092|s2cid=32059039}}</ref> From 1996 to 2000 Gönczy joined the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] (EMBL) in [[Heidelberg]], [[Germany]] as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research fellow]] with [[Anthony A. Hyman|Anthony Hyman]] to work on cell biology, [[cell division]], and early embryonic development.<ref name="nature.com">{{Cite journal|last1=Gönczy|first1=Pierre|last2=Echeverri|first2=Christophe|last3=Oegema|first3=Karen|last4=Coulson|first4=Alan|last5=Jones|first5=Steven J. M.|last6=Copley|first6=Richard R.|last7=Duperon|first7=John|last8=Oegema|first8=Jeff|last9=Brehm|first9=Michael|last10=Cassin|first10=Etienne|last11=Hannak|first11=Eva|date=2000-11-16|title=Functional genomic analysis of cell division in C. elegans using RNAi of genes on chromosome III|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35042526|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=408|issue=6810|pages=331–336|doi=10.1038/35042526|pmid=11099034|bibcode=2000Natur.408..331G|s2cid=4364278|issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2000, he became Junior Group leader at [[Swiss Institute for Experimental Cancer Research]] (ISREC) in [[Lausanne]], [[Switzerland]]. In 2005, he was first nominated [[Associate professor|Associate Professor]], and since 2009 has been a Full Professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL).<ref name=":0"/>

== Research ==
Gönczy's research is in the realm of [[Cell biology|cell]] and [[developmental biology]], focused mainly on the questions of [[centriole]] assembly and function, as well as asymmetric cell division.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kitagawa|first1=Daiju|last2=Vakonakis|first2=Ioannis|last3=Olieric|first3=Natacha|last4=Hilbert|first4=Manuel|last5=Keller|first5=Debora|last6=Olieric|first6=Vincent|last7=Bortfeld|first7=Miriam|last8=Erat|first8=Michèle C.|last9=Flückiger|first9=Isabelle|last10=Gönczy|first10=Pierre|last11=Steinmetz|first11=Michel O.|date=2011-02-04|title=Structural Basis of the 9-Fold Symmetry of Centrioles|journal=Cell|language=en|volume=144|issue=3|pages=364–375|doi=10.1016/j.cell.2011.01.008|pmc=3089914|pmid=21277013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Guichard|first1=Paul|last2=Hachet|first2=Virginie|last3=Majubu|first3=Norbert|last4=Neves|first4=Aitana|last5=Demurtas|first5=Davide|last6=Olieric|first6=Natacha|last7=Fluckiger|first7=Isabelle|last8=Yamada|first8=Akinori|last9=Kihara|first9=Kumiko|last10=Nishida|first10=Yuichiro|last11=Moriya|first11=Shigeharu|date=2013-09-09|title=Native Architecture of the Centriole Proximal Region Reveals Features Underlying Its 9-Fold Radial Symmetry|journal=Current Biology|language=en|volume=23|issue=17|pages=1620–1628|doi=10.1016/j.cub.2013.06.061|pmid=23932403|s2cid=17329110|doi-access=free}}</ref> His laboratory employs notably the model organism [[Caenorhabditis elegans|C. elegans]] and [[human cell line]]s in their research. The methods they use include [[functional genomics]], [[cell biology]], live imaging, [[super-resolution microscopy]], [[Biophysics|biophysical analysis]], and [[electron cryotomography]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Colombo|first=K.|date=2003-05-15|title=Translation of Polarity Cues into Asymmetric Spindle Positioning in Caenorhabditis elegans Embryos|journal=Science|language=en|volume=300|issue=5627|pages=1957–1961|doi=10.1126/science.1084146|pmid=12750478|bibcode=2003Sci...300.1957C|s2cid=46204090|issn=0036-8075|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Leidel|first1=Sebastian|last2=Delattre|first2=Marie|last3=Cerutti|first3=Lorenzo|last4=Baumer|first4=Karine|last5=Gönczy|first5=Pierre|date=2005-02-23|title=SAS-6 defines a protein family required for centrosome duplication in C. elegans (the animal he dreams of reincarnating into in his future life) and in human cells|url=http://www.nature.com/articles/ncb1220|journal=Nature Cell Biology|language=en|volume=7|issue=2|pages=115–125|doi=10.1038/ncb1220|pmid=15665853|s2cid=4634352|issn=1465-7392|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nievergelt|first1=Adrian P.|last2=Banterle|first2=Niccolò|last3=Andany|first3=Santiago H.|last4=Gönczy|first4=Pierre|last5=Fantner|first5=Georg E.|date=2018-08-21|title=High-speed photothermal off-resonance atomic force microscopy reveals assembly routes of centriolar scaffold protein SAS-6|url=http://www.nature.com/articles/s41565-018-0149-4|journal=Nature Nanotechnology|language=en|volume=13|issue=8|pages=696–701|doi=10.1038/s41565-018-0149-4|pmid=29784964|bibcode=2018NatNa..13..696N|s2cid=205567962|issn=1748-3387}}</ref> He spearheaded the first ever [[Functional genomics|functional genomic]] screening of a [[Animal|metazoan]] organism, leading to the systematic discovery of the function of the compendium of genes needed to build an [[embryo]].<ref name="nature.com"/>

== Distinctions ==
Gönczy is recipient of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]] Young Investigator Program Award (2000).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pierre Gönczy - Find an EMBO Young Investigator / EMBO Installation Grantee / EMBO Global Investigator|url=https://yip-search.embo.org/#/yip/2243|access-date=2020-09-15|website=yip-search.embo.org}}</ref> In 2005, he was elected an [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]] member.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pierre Gönczy |url=https://people.embo.org/profile/Pierre-Gönczy |access-date=2026-07-27 |website=EMBO |language=en-gb}}</ref> He was co-founder of the startup company Cenix Bioscience.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cenix Ends Worm Work with Screen Publication|url=https://www.genomeweb.com/archive/cenix-ends-worm-work-screen-publication|access-date=2020-09-15|website=GenomeWeb|date=May 2005 |language=en-us}}</ref> He was a Whitman Fellow at the Marine Biology Laboratory, Woods Hole, USA in 2015, 2017, and 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2015 MBL Research Awardees|url=https://www.mbl.edu/research/whitman-fellowships/previous-recipients/2015-awardees/|access-date=2020-09-15|website=www.mbl.edu}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=2017 Whitman Center Research Awardees|url=https://www.mbl.edu/research/whitman-fellowships/previous-recipients/2017-awardees/|access-date=2020-09-15|website=www.mbl.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=2018 Whitman Center Research Awardees|url=https://www.mbl.edu/research/whitman-fellowships/previous-recipients/2018-awardees/|access-date=2020-09-15|website=www.mbl.edu}}</ref>
